headline: Council confirms votes on Draper Laboratories tax break, parking, and land deals in Hamilton Canal District.
summary: Public speakers split on the Draper deal, with some asking for enforceable job and community benefit terms, and union members backing it after a labor agreement was reached that day. The council also set the fiscal year 2027 minimum residential factor and cancelled its December 1 and December 29 meetings. A motion for a report on cannabis consumption lounges failed, 3-7.
decisions: Approved cancelling the December 1 and December 29, 2026 council meetings, 10-0.
Confirmed executive session votes on a parking agreement, tax increment financing, and right of first refusal with Draper Laboratories, 10-0.
Approved the fiscal year 2027 minimum residential factor of 0.899590, 10-0.
Referred a Boston Gas request to replace a gas main at 61 Durant Street to the wire inspector, with three similar utility requests.
Failed 3-7 a request for a report on possible cannabis consumption lounges in Lowell.
Approved asking the city manager to find a way to improve lighting in the Greenhalge School gymnasium.
Approved asking the city manager to arrange a discussion between the Lowell Housing Authority and the City Council.
Approved asking the city manager to add warning markers on newly created sidewalk extensions.
Approved asking the city manager to study whether the North Common Park basketball court lights can come on an hour earlier.
Approved asking the city manager for a plan to prevent illegal dumping at the Cupples Square parking lot and an update on security cameras.
Approved spending a $35,640 fire grant and a $75,000 MassDEP grant, and authorized contracts with TEC, Inc., 10-0.
Referred three MSBA loan orders for school window projects to a December 7 public hearing.
Referred an ordinance to amend the cemetery fee schedule to a November 24, 2026 public hearing.
Referred a property damage claim to the Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred a request for a handicapped parking sign at 20 Wight Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred three gas main and electric conduit requests, including one at 681 Merrimack Street, to a November 24 public hearing.
discussion: Draper benefits enforcement: Speakers said the community commitments were not in the binding agreement and asked for enforceable terms, including local jobs and a community benefits agreement.
Labor agreement: A labor agreement reached at 12:30 that day added local hiring goals, apprenticeship requirements, and workforce targets for Lowell residents, minorities, and women.
Cannabis consumption lounges: Members debated whether to study the lounges, citing economic development on one side and potency, driving, and neighborhood concerns on the other.
Environmental impacts: Speakers asked for public review of air emissions, energy use, and other effects of the Draper project before final approval.
